value.title: Fast seat cards: /v1/state in milliseconds, a bulk read, and the note's timestamp
value.summary: Chainglass (the UI) now seeds every seat's card from /v1/state on start instead of replaying the event log. One call takes 1.3 to 3.7 s, calls seem to run one at a time (4 in flight: about 6.5 s each), and seeding 84 seats took 136 s. The card also gives `stateNote` without when it was written.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Reported by the chainglass prime pij-lonely-antelope on 2026-11-02, measured against the live daemon; the prime re-measured `pij-rs --json state <seat>` at 1.32–1.33 s with the daemon otherwise idle (pid 67958, 10% CPU, 35 MB). The handler (crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs, around state_card at :2860 and the held-delivery projection above it) reads registry, liveness, the latest card, the latest state record and held deliveries; at least one of those reads appears to scan the 4.16M-row spine per call. Asks: (1) one call fast, and concurrent calls not serialised; (2) a bulk read, all seats' cards in one call or the card fields on /v1/seats; (3) `stateNote`'s timestamp and cursor, like `statusAt`/`statusSeq`. Chainglass is another repo (read-only): ~/substrate/chainglass apps/web/src/features/089-first-class-pij/server/rs/start-pij-poller.ts and rs-client.ts. Rulings: assets/rulings.md.

sections.name: goals
value: One /v1/state call takes milliseconds, not seconds, whatever the spine size.
Concurrent card reads don't queue behind each other.
A client can read every seat's card in one call.
The card says when its state note was written.

sections.name: non_goals
value: Deleting or compacting spine rows (that is a separate ruling).
Changing the meaning of any existing card field.

value.claim: Diagnosis. Profile one /v1/state call on a private daemon with a spine shaped like the live one (about 4M rows), and name which reads cost the time and why concurrent calls serialise (a single sqlite connection, a lock, a full scan). Record query plans (EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN) for each read. Write assets/evidence/diagnosis.md and send the prime a pointer before fixing.
value.note: Proven: three full spine scans per card via tail's OR; concurrency = competing full scans, not a lock. assets/evidence/diagnosis.md.

value.claim: Fast single read. Each read behind /v1/state is an indexed lookup bounded by the seat's own rows (or a cached projection with an explicit invalidation rule), so one call on the 4M-row seed takes a stated bound in milliseconds. The card's content is byte-for-byte the same as main's for every seat on the seed (a golden comparison over all seats), including held deliveries. 4 concurrent calls each finish within a stated bound.
value.note: Proven: indexed reads bounded by the seat's rows (store/src/spine.rs:48,60; core/src/report.rs:311); single 1.7-5.2 ms, 3.59M-row seat <=5 ms, 4 concurrent <=7.2 ms each; 1,893/1,893 cards identical to main incl. held (lg-0004).

value.claim: Bulk read. One call returns every local seat's card (a new endpoint or a `cards` option on an existing one; state which, with the reason), with the same per-seat content as /v1/state, in a stated bound on the seed. Document it in docs/how/pij-rs-api.md; additive, no existing field changes.
value.note: Proven: new GET /v1/cards (daemon/src/http/mod.rs:2715), same seat_card builder as /v1/state; a new route because /v1/seats is polled by federation and rosters that need no card reads; 86 cards in 49-64 ms; bulk==single tests; docs/how/pij-rs-api.md.

value.claim: Note timestamp. The card gains `stateNoteAt` (epoch ms) and `stateNoteSeq` (spine cursor) for the report.state note, null when there is no note, matching how `statusAt`/`statusSeq` work. Additive; golden fixtures updated; docs.
value.note: Proven: stateNoteAt/stateNoteSeq from the report.state record (daemon/src/http/mod.rs:2946, types.rs:591), null with no note; golden golden/api/state-card.json; docs.

value.claim: Cost (AGENTS.md § Resource cost). No new loop, poll or launch site. If you add a cache, state its lifetime and invalidation, and its memory per seat. Backpressure row: reads per card, rows touched per read. Private before/after timings; the prime takes the deployed reading.
value.note: Live (prime, pid 97258): /v1/state 1.73-1.74 s -> 0.01-0.87 s cold (session fold), 0.00-0.03 s warm; /v1/cards 88 cards 1.31 s cold, 0.055 s warm, 0 unavailable; daemon 10.6% CPU, 197 MB. No new loop, timer or launch site; no new cache (the session source's existing per-seat cursor cache is warmed per bound seat). Cost row bp-0002; private before/after lg-0005.

value.claim: Proof. Each behaviour change has a test RED on main (quoted) and green on the branch. Mutants: a read falls back to a spine scan; bulk and single cards diverge; note timestamp taken from the wrong record; stale cache after a new report. Each turns a test red, then is restored. Scoped cargo tests, clippy -D warnings, fmt; CI green on the exact head. Anything not run is NOT RUN with its reason.
value.note: Proven: 5 tests red on main (lg-0002), 8/8 mutants killed (lg-0006), scoped tests/clippy/fmt (lg-0003), CI green (lg-0007).

value.title: Make card reads fast, add a bulk card read and the state note's time
value.brief: One phase: profile /v1/state, make one call fast and concurrent calls independent, add a bulk read for every seat's card, add stateNoteAt/stateNoteSeq, docs, cost, mutants, PR. CS 3.
